note: Author notes keyed by objId. Rendered under an (n) icon next to the (i) info icon on the slide caption.

Jupiter.en: This image was taken in Purcellville at a soccer stadium. You can see Jupiter and several of its Galilean moons here — Io, Europa, Ganymede, and Callisto.

M10.en: The M 56 and M 10 clusters were taken during the Canadian wildfires, making it extremely difficult to picture these bodies. The image processing pipeline was stress-tested under these conditions.

M16.en: The famous Pillars of Creation live inside this nebula — you just have to look deep into the centre to spot them.

M24.en: M 24 sits in the same crowded Sagittarius arm as the Milky Way's galactic centre — they're about 13° apart though, so the centre itself isn't in this frame, but you're aimed at one of the densest star fields in the sky. The black streaks aren't dust lanes — they're tree branches that got in the way of the shot.

M51.en: This photo was taken at the ditch behind my house. A skunk was out there and approached me until I flashed it with a flashlight.

M56.en: The M 56 and M 10 clusters were taken during the Canadian wildfires, making it extremely difficult to picture these bodies. The image processing pipeline was stress-tested under these conditions.

M63.en: Zoom in on this galaxy and you can pick out the little yellow rings — layered dust lanes wrapping the spiral arms.

M8.en: This image was taken in the front yard with street lights close by. A fox approached me as I was taking this photo, and a tree cut the exposure time short.

MilkyWay.en: There was too much light pollution to get any sort of detail of the Milky Way in this picture. This was my best attempt in a Bortle 5 area.

NGC6826.en: This planetary nebula only resolves as a little green star on my S30 — the shell is too small (~25 arcsec) to show detail at this focal length.

NGC7000.en: One of my favorite photos and one of the first mosaic photos taken of the sky.

NGC7023.en: The reason you can't see many stars around this nebula is that there's a lot of dark absorption nebulosity surrounding the central reflection nebula. A much longer exposure would bring out those dark structures.

Saturn.en: The exposure on this planet was too long for any resolution on detail.

Thuban.en: Thuban and Draco don't actually have galaxy-like features — this was one of my first photos using the S30 Pro, and I didn't quite have a steady surface or much knowledge yet, so there was some shaking.

UMa.en: This image was taken on a slightly cloudy night. Notice all the streaks in the sky if you look closely — those are satellites reflecting the sun's light back at us.
